sc_mini_south_face.blurb: Mini South Face is a small cliff within Table Rock State Park near Pumpkintown, sitting just to the right of the spot where the newer CCC Trail meets the rock. It is shorter than the big walls around it and tends to stay damp, with seepage common on its cracks. Most of the 13 routes are trad, with a few bolted sport lines mixed in, and the grades run from 5.7 up to 5.10, split fairly evenly between the 5.8 and 5.10 ranges. The natural crack and feature lines recall a scaled-down version of a larger south-facing wall. A faint path leads in from the trail, dropping below a short wall.

ut_cobrazone.blurb: Cobrazone is a quiet crag high on Bald Mountain in the Uinta Mountains of northeast Utah, at roughly 10,800 feet. Its routes mostly face east, so it gets sun in the morning and cools off by evening. The 13 climbs are a blend of trad, sport and alpine-style lines, some of them two pitches, with grades from 5.8 into the 5.11 range and the bulk sitting around 5.9 to 5.10. A broad ledge partway up serves as a handy base. Expect a short walk over talus from the trailhead and far fewer people than at the busier Wasatch crags.

ut_the_weasel_formation.blurb: The Weasel Formation is a cluster of large walls and freestanding towers in the northern San Rafael Swell, on the north side of I-70 in central Utah. The rock is sandstone, and the climbing is mostly crack-based trad, with a couple of aid routes among the 13 recorded lines. Free grades run from 5.8 to 5.11, with most around 5.9. Several of the lines go up spires with distinctive summits, so expect a desert-tower feel and some route-finding. The way in is a talus hike from the end of the dirt road up to the base of the formation.

ut_bug_barn_dance_wall.blurb: Bug Barn Dance Wall is a moderate limestone crag in Rock Canyon above Provo, on the north side of the canyon near the stream. All 13 routes are bolted sport lines, and nearly all sit between 5.10 and 5.11, with a single 5.9 to warm up on, so it suits climbers who are comfortable leading 5.10. The rock is solid and offers good edges, and a roof system breaks up the middle of the main face. It gets a lot of afternoon sun. Some loose, chossy ground is crossed on the way to the base.

ut_gate_boulder.blurb: Gate Boulder is a big boulder in the Gate Boulders group in Little Cottonwood Canyon, close to the road and relatively cool. It has 13 problems, and the moderate end is the draw: a tall west face holds a variety of slab problems, with a handful of easy classics near V0. Most of the rest fall between V3 and V4, with one V6 and a single top-end problem near V9 for the strong. Climbing goes all the way around the boulder, which makes it a good stop for a mixed-ability group working a circuit.

ut_wasp_the.blurb: The Wasp is a small spire on the north side of the mouth of Rock Canyon, east of Provo, reached up the same gully as Trilogy Buttress. It holds 13 routes, nearly all of them bolted sport lines plus one trad route, with grades from 5.7 to 5.11 and the largest group around 5.10. Traffic is light, so the holds are not polished. The slope at the base is steep and loose, so take care not to send debris onto people below. A past rockfall reshaped part of the formation.

_skipped.ut_wave_wall_the: Only one fetched page (the Mountain Project crag page) is about this wall; the other Big Cottonwood page that mentions a wave wall lists a different set of routes in the Smoots Dugway area, so it could not be matched to these coordinates.
_skipped.ut_sunny_side_the: No fetched page is about the Mill Creek (Moab) Sunny Side itself; the Mountain Project Sunny Side pages found are in New Mexico and southwest Utah, and the Mill Creek parent page only lists it.

_conflicts.ut_wasp_the: Stored rock is quartzite; the Mountain Project Glacial Obsession route page (https://www.mountainproject.com/route/106135387/glacial-obsession) describes the lower rock as glacially deposited tillite, while the Rock Canyon page says quartzite near the mouth. Rock not named in the blurb.
_conflicts.ut_bug_barn_dance_wall: Stored aspect is W; the crag page (https://mountainproject.com/area/105739404/bug-barn-dance-wall) says mainly south with some west exposure. Aspect left unchanged.
_conflicts.sc_mini_south_face: Stored rock is gneiss; the Pumpkintown overview page (https://carolinaclimbers.org/climbing-areas/pumpkintown-sc.html) calls the cliff granite, but it does not name this face. Rock not named in the blurb.
